title: Perfect Week
cn: 第 14 集 · 完美一周
novel:
Barney declared it would be his "Perfect Week" — seven women in seven days, no [[rejections|rejection]]. The gang watched with [[dread|dread]] and a little [[admiration|admiration]].

"You're [[jinxing|jinx]] it," Lily warned. "Don't talk about a [[streak|streak]] before it ends."

But Barney was [[superstitious|superstitious]] in all the wrong ways. He wore the same socks. He refused to wash his lucky [[tie|tie]]. He [[challenged|challenge]] fate at every turn.

Lily and Marshall tried to [[distract|distract]] him. They invited him to dinner, to a movie, to a long walk. Nothing worked. Barney [[persisted|persist]].

By Sunday, he had done it. Seven for seven. The bar [[erupted|erupt]] in celebration. Barney raised his glass, [[triumphant|triumphant]] — and then immediately [[knocked|knock]] it over.

Some victories, Ted reflected, were so [[fragile|fragile]] that even a spilled drink could [[shatter|shatter]] them. But Barney did not care. He had his Perfect Week, and no one could take that away — not even himself.

rejection.en: when someone refuses to accept you

dread.en: a strong feeling of fear about the future

admiration.en: a feeling of respect for someone

jinx.en: to bring bad luck by talking about it

streak.en: a series of successes in a row

tie.en: a piece of cloth worn around the neck with a suit

persist.en: to keep doing something despite difficulty

erupt.en: to suddenly begin, often with noise

knock.en: to hit something so it falls
